scope: Bounded source-derived KMBUS_EEPROM_READ 0x43 block-map probe on local WB2A / VDensHO1 / 20C2.
strong_observations: All 13 exact source-derived address/length shapes returned normal successful 0x43 responses.
0x0001/1 returned 0x88 identically in three immediate repeats.
0x0078/5 returned 5498549854 and 0x0078/8 returned 5498549854985498; the shorter result is exactly the prefix of the longer result and both are repetitions/truncations of the same two-byte word 5498.
0x006A/6 and 0x0070/7 also show the same 5498 repeated/truncated pattern.
0x00A0/10, 0x00AA/10 and 0x00B4/10 all returned the exact same 10-byte payload 54985498549854985498 despite representing three distinct source blocks.
Odd-address 0x0083/4 returned 97549754 and 0x0091/1 returned 97, which is consistent with a phase-shifted two-byte-pattern hypothesis, but that mechanism is not yet proven.
Low blocks 0x0001, 0x000A and 0x000F do not follow the 5498 repetition pattern and remain candidates for a distinct/stable region.
interpretation_boundary: A successful 0x43 response does not by itself prove that the returned bytes are literal EEPROM contents.
The repeated two-byte pattern reproduces the same structural pathology previously observed in prefix-less 0x43/F8 reads. Therefore the 13/13 success must not be described as a validated EEPROM dump.

The current experiment proves that frames carrying PrefixRead=030000000101 are accepted. It does not yet prove that the controller actually uses those six bytes as a routing selector, because no same-address prefixed-vs-prefixless A/B control has been performed.
The GWG_BT2/LGM27 source semantics must not be assigned to local WB2A data unless separately correlated.
next_step: Perform same-address P-N-P comparisons (prefixed, no-prefix, prefixed) on a very small fixed set: 0x0001/1, 0x000A/5, 0x0078/8, 0x00A0/10.
Use the P-N-P pattern to distinguish real PrefixRead routing from ignored/irrelevant extra bytes while controlling for the known dynamic two-byte result.
Only if PrefixRead has a reproducible effect should the 0x43 path be interpreted as routed subordinate EEPROM access.
